principles.statement: Deliver in slices that each stand alone and work end-to-end.
principles.rationale: A vertical slice that runs — however thin — proves the architecture and gives something to iterate; horizontal layers prove nothing until the last one lands.

principles.statement: Every increment leaves the system in a working state.
principles.rationale: A branch that 'needs one more week before it runs again' has silently accumulated every mistake made during that week.

principles.statement: Feedback from a working increment corrects the plan for the next one.
principles.rationale: The plan made before the first slice was built had the least information it will ever have.

heuristics.name: Walking skeleton first
heuristics.description: Build the thinnest end-to-end path (one input, one output, real wiring) before thickening any layer.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Starting any new system, service, or pipeline.
examples: One file flowing through parse→store→serve beats a perfect parser with no sink.

heuristics.name: Stop-and-integrate check
heuristics.description: If the current increment can't land within the session/day, cut its scope until it can.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Any increment crossing a time boundary.
examples: 'Half the feature, fully working' integrates; 'the whole feature, half-working' does not.

decision_rules.condition: An increment is stuck and growing without reaching a runnable state.
decision_rules.action: Cut scope to the smallest runnable slice; stash the rest as the next increment's plan.

decision_rules.condition: New information from a landed increment contradicts the original plan.
decision_rules.action: Re-plan the remaining increments — do not push through a plan the feedback has invalidated.
